carefully and the concentration of the additive must be regularly checked. Hardness The total hardness of the water is the combined effect of the temporary and permanent hardness. The proportion of calcium and magnesium salts is of overriding importance. The temporary hardness is determined by the carbon- ate content of the calcium and magnesium salts. The permanent hardness is determined by the amount of remaining calcium and magnesium salts (sulph- ates). The temporary (carbonate) hardness is the critical factor that determines the extent of limescale deposit in the cooling system. Water with a total hardness of > 10°dGH must be mixed with distilled water or softened. Subsequent hardening of extremely soft water is only necessary to prevent foaming if emulsifiable slushing oils are used.

Engine cooling water specifications Preliminary remarks As is also the case with the fuel and lubricating oil, the engine cooling water must be carefully selected, handled and checked. If this is not the case, cor- rosion, erosion and cavitation may occur at the walls of the cooling system in contact with water and deposits may form. Deposits obstruct the transfer of heat and can cause thermal overloading of the cooled parts. The system must be treated with an anticorrosive agent before bringing it into operation for the first time. The concentrations prescribed by the engine manufacturer must always be observed during subsequent operation. The above especially applies if a chemical additive is added. Regular checks of the cooling water condition and cooling water system Treated cooling water may become contaminated when the engine is in operation, which causes the additive to loose some of its effectiveness. It is therefore advisable to regularly check the cooling system and the cooling water condition. To determine leakages in the lube oil system, it is advisable to carry out regular checks of water in the compensating tank. Indications of oil content in water are, e.g. discoloration or a visible oil film on the surface of the water sample. The additive concentration must be checked at least once a week using the test kits specified by the manufacturer. The results must be documented. Concentrations of chemical additives The chemical additive concentrations shall not be less than the minimum concentrations indicated in the table „Nitrite-containing chemical additives“.

Specification of engine coolant Preliminary remarks An engine coolant is composed as follows: water for heat removal and cool- ant additive for corrosion protection. As is also the case with the fuel and lubricating oil, the engine coolant must be carefully selected, handled and checked. If this is not the case, corrosion, erosion and cavitation may occur at the walls of the cooling system in con- tact with water and deposits may form. Deposits obstruct the transfer of heat and can cause thermal overloading of the cooled parts. The system must be treated with an anticorrosive agent before bringing it into operation for the first time. The concentrations prescribed by the engine manufacturer must always be observed during subsequent operation. The above especially applies if a chemical additive is added.

冷却液污染与沉积风险
As is also the case with the fuel and lubricating oil, the engine coolant must be carefully selected, handled and checked. If this is not the case, corrosion, erosion and cavitation may occur at the walls of the cooling system in contact with water and deposits may form. Deposits obstruct the transfer of heat and can cause thermal overloading of the cooled parts. The system must be treated with an anticorrosive agent before bringing it into operation for the first time. The concentrations prescribed by the engine manufacturer must always be observed during subsequent operation. The above especially applies if a chemical additive is added. Temperatures and pressures will vary between engines and with changing operating conditions, temperatures, and lIf coolant temperature rises above the maximum coolant temperature, reduce load on engine. Unless temperature drops quickly, stop engine and determine cause before resuming operation. Stop engine as soon as possible if there are any signs of part failure. To protect the environment, please dispose of used or leftover chemicals at a properly designated disposal site for destruction. Cooling system There is a risk of flooding when working on the sea- water system. Turn off the engine and close the sea cock (where installed) before starting work on the sys- tem. Avoid opening the coolant filler cap when the engine is hot. Steam or hot coolant can spray out and cause burns. If work must be carried out with the engine at operat- ing temperature and the coolant filler cap or a cock open or a coolant hose disconnected, open the cool- ant filler cap carefully and slowly to release pressure before removing the cap completely. Note that the coolant may still be hot and can cause burns. Lubrication system Hot oil can cause burns.

Cavitation of the cylinder wall begins when air bubbles remove the wall's protective oxide film. Flexing of the cylinder wall after the fuel mixture explodes in the combustion chamber causes cylinder wall vibration and creates air bubbles in the coolant. Concentration of air bubbles increases when cooling system pressure is low or when the system leaks. Also, increased vibration amplifies the quantity of air bubbles. Vibration multiplies when the engine is run cold, because of increased piston-to-cylinder clearance. Vibration also multiplies when the engine is lugged. These air bubbles form on the outside of the cylinder wall (perpendicular to the wrist pin) and then explode inward (implode). When air bubbles continue to implode, sufficient energy is released to physically attack the cylinder wall and remove the oxide film. Corrosion and pitting then take place at a high rate.

Engine Overcooling Overcooling can damage an engine just as overheating can. Overcooling occurs when the normal temperature at which the engine operates cannot be reached. This condition is most severe with the use of high sulfur fuel. High sulfur fuel increases wear if the temperature is not over 80°C (175°F). Overcooling is the result of coolant bypassing the water temperature regulators and flowing directly to the radiator. Causes of Overcooling Low ambient air temperature and light load application conditions may exist when overcooling occurs. A defective temperature gauge can give an indication of overcooling. The gauge can be checked for accuracy by comparing the actual temperature of the coolant in the water temperature regulator housing with the temperature indication on the gauge.

source_document: S06 Scania DI16 船用发动机车主手册（中文）
text:
冷却液（乙二醇-水混合液）：冰点温度与乙二醇体积比对应关系如下：乙二醇体积比15%时，开始形成冰泥的温度为-6°C；乙二醇体积比20%时，开始形成冰泥的温度为-9°C；乙二醇体积比25%时，开始形成冰泥的温度为-12°C；乙二醇体积比30%时，开始形成冰泥的温度为-16°C；乙二醇体积比35%时，开始形成冰泥的温度为-21°C；乙二醇体积比40%时，开始形成冰泥的温度为-24°C；乙二醇体积比45%时，开始形成冰泥的温度为-30°C；乙二醇体积比50%时，开始形成冰泥的温度为-37°C。适用条件：冷却系统容量单位为dm³（升）。

冷却液防腐剂比例
检查防腐剂 冷却液中必须始终有足够的防腐剂，以便为冷却系统提供防腐保护。 如果不存在结冰危险，则仅应在冷却液中使用 Scania Corrosion Inhibitor （Scania 防腐剂）。 Scania Corrosion Inhibitor （Scania 防腐剂）中的抑制剂不含亚硝酸盐。 防腐剂的正确体积比为 8-12%。

heavy deposits of dirt and metallic particles (i.e. rust and chips, etc.) are found everywhere in the system where it is allowed to rest by the circulating cooling water. Fresh water treatment The engine cooling water is, like fuel oil and lubricating oil, a medium which must be carefully selected, treated, maintained and monitored. Otherwise, corrosion, corrosion fatigue and cavitation may occur on the sur- faces of the cooling system which are in contact with the water, and deposits may form. Corrosion and cavitation may reduce the life time and safety factors of parts concerned, and deposits will impair the heat transfer and may result in thermal overload of the components to be cooled. The treatment process of the cooling water has to be effected before the first commission of the plant, i.e. immediately after installation at the shipyard or at the power plant.

Over a period of time, the concentration of coolant additives is depleted. This depletion occurs because additives deplete during the coating of metal surfaces, and from continuously neutralizing acids that form in the system. Therefore, to maintain constant protection, it is necessary to periodically replenish the additive concentration. Either replace the initial precharge element with the maintenance element or add 0.47 liter (1 pint) of additive for every 75.8 liters (20 U.S. gallons) of coolant at recommended intervals. Normal recommended intervals are 16,000 to 19,000 kilometers (10,000 to 12,000 miles), or at 250 Service Meter Hours.

The temporary (carbonate) hardness is the critical factor that deter- mines the extent of limescale deposit in the cooling system. Water with a total hardness of > 10°dGH must be mixed with distilled water or softened. • Temperature Control: The heat exchanger must be capable of delivering the proper amount of cooling, proportional to engine load. • Load Control: The amount of external water flow through a Cat Engine is directly proportional to the engine’s load. The greater the load, the greater the amount of cooling required and the more water the engine’s internal cooling circuitry will discharge for cooling. At light loads, the engine’s temperature controls will bypass the external portion of the engine cooling system, recirculating virtually all of the coolant. If the water pressure presented to an engine by a central cooling system is too high, the proper operation of the engine’s temperature controls may be overridden, and the engine will suffer over or under cooling problems.

source_document: S39 MAN L21/31 Project Guide
text:
中央冷却系统总体组成：MAN Energy Solutions B 52 00 0 L21/31;L27/38, 2016.09.28 - Diesel-electrical propulsion plants。适用条件：外部预热系统，项目39。高压来自外部冷却水泵可能干扰发动机预热；为避免此情况，多数情况下需在冷却水进口安装自动截止阀，该阀在发动机停止时关闭。外部预热器容量应为3.0-3.5 kW/缸。流过发动机的流量：每缸约4 l/min（自上而下流动）和25 l/min（自下而上流动）。中央冷却系统的不同布置有多种变化，可讨论以适应船东或建造商的特定要求。

中央冷却系统总体组成：MAN Energy Solutions B 52 00 0 L27/38;L21/31, 2016.09.28 - Diesel-electrical propulsion plants 7 (8) Data for external preheating system, item 39 High pressure from external cooling water pumps may disturb the preheating of the engine. In order to avoid this, it is in most cases necessary to install automatic shut off valve at cooling water inlet, which close when the engine is stopped. The capacity of the external preheater should be 3.0-3.5 kW/cyl. The flow through the engine should for each cylinder be approx. 4 l/min with flow from top and downwards and 25 l/min with flow from bottom and upwards. Different arrangements of central cooling systems There are many variations of centralised cooling systems and we are available to discuss various changes to suit an owner’s or builder’s specific wishes.

text:
淡水侧系统组成：Stage 2 of the two-stage charge air coolers (HE-040/041)；Lube oil cooler, free-standing (HE-002)；Nozzle cooling water cooler (HE-005)；Fuel oil cooler (HE-007)；Gearbox lube oil cooler (HE-023) (or e.g. alternator cooling in case of an electric propulsion plant)；Cooler for LT cooling water (HE-024)；Fuel oil cooler, supply circuit (HE-025) (if applicable, see section External fuel system – Residual fuel (HFO) supply system, Page 425)；Other components, for example, auxiliary engines (GenSets)。适用条件：LT cooling water pumps can be either of engine driven or electrically driven type. In case an engine driven LT pump is used and no electric driven pump (LT main pump) is installed in the LT circuit, an LT circulation pump has to be installed.

LT circulation pump：capacity approximately 8 m³/h for L engines, 12 m³/h for V engines at 1.5 bar pressure head。适用条件：We recommend an electric driven pump.

text:
淡水侧系统组成
▪ Lube oil cooler, free-standing (HE-002) ▪ Nozzle cooling water cooler (HE-005) ▪ Fuel oil cooler (HE-007) ▪ Gearbox lube oil cooler (HE-023) (or e.g. alternator cooling in case of an electric propulsion plant) ▪ Cooler for LT cooling water (HE-024) ▪ Fuel oil cooler, supply circuit (HE-025) (if applicable, see section External fuel system – Heavy fuel oil (HFO) supply system, Page 388 ) ▪ Other components such as e.g. auxiliary engines (GenSets) LT cooling water pumps can be either of engine driven or electrically driven type. The block is a closed circuit contained on the engine; therefore, only the water returning to the aftercooler pump requires a cooling source. text:
高温冷却水系统组成：发动机类型仅限L16/24、L21/31和L27/38连续运行。适用条件：参见B 12 07 0，预润滑泵。预热器控制用于控制安装在发动机上的电加热器，在停机期间预热发动机缸套冷却水。在机柜正面有一个“加热器开启”指示灯和一个关闭/自动开关。此外，加热元件有过载保护。温度通过安装在公共高温出口管中的开/关恒温器控制。此外，控制系统确保仅在发动机停机时激活加热器。该箱还包括电动盘车装置的控制。正面有一个“运行”指示灯和一个开/关电源开关。盘车装置的控制配备有用于正向和反向的两个接触器。

text:
高温冷却水系统组成：HT冷却水预热模块（MOD-004）在冷机启动前，需将水套预热至发动机出口最低60°C；从10°C预热至60°C所需总加热功率（4小时内）见加热功率表（第379页）；发动机类型 L/V 发动机；最小加热功率 14 kW/缸；适用条件：表158：加热功率，这些值包括发动机外表面的辐射热损失，并已考虑冷却系统20%的热损失裕度；为防止发动机加热过快和不均匀，HT冷却水预热温度在发动机入口处必须强制低于90°C，循环量不得超过额定流量的30%；最大加热功率需据此计算。

A secondary function of the preheater is to provide heat capacity in the HT cooling water system during engine part load operation. This is required for marine propulsion plants with a high freshwater requirement, e.g. on passen- ger vessels, where frequent load changes are common. For engines operated in arctic conditions or with charge air from outside the vessel, the capacity of the preheater has to be increased. In this case contact Everllence. It is also required for arrangements with an additional charge air preheating by deviation of HT cooling water to the charge air cooler stage 2 (HE-008). In this case the heat output of the preheater is to be increased by approximately 50%. Avoid an installation of the preheater in parallel to the engine driven HT-pump. In this case, the preheater may not be operated while the engine is running.

The charge air temperature control CHATCO reduces the amount of con- densed water that accumulates during engine operation under tropical condi- tions. HT cooling water circuit General The HT cooling water system consists of the following coolers and heat ex- changers: ▪ Charge air coolers stage 1 ( HE-038/039 ) ▪ Cylinder cooling ▪ Cooler for HT cooling water (HE-003) ▪ Heat utilisation, e.g. fresh water generator (HE-026) ▪ HT cooling water preheating module (MOD-004) The HT cooling water pumps can be either of engine-driven or electrically- driven type. The outlet temperature of the cylinder cooling water at the engine varies between 88°C and 100°C, depending on the engine load and intake air temperature. The maximum outlet temperature is limited to 100°C for standard applica- tions. It may be released to max. 106°C for waste heat recovery use.

Heat Recovery (Cabin Heater) Caterpillar does not offer a heat recovery system or cabin heater options. If aftermarket system is required Caterpillar recommends installing shut off valves on the supply and return lines from the engine to the system. The valve seat, disk, and stem must be made from corrosion resistant material such as monel alloys. Seawater Strainers Strainers are required in order to protect the seawater pump, aftercooler, heat exchanger and other cooling system components from foreign material in the seawater. The foreign material can plug and/or coat heat transfer surfaces, causing overheating of the engine and shortened life of components. If the foreign material is abrasive, it will erode pump impellers and soft metal parts, reducing their effectiveness. Seawater strainers should be installed below the water line and as close to the seawater inlet or sea chest as possible.

Heat Transfer Heat transfer describes the tendency of heat to move from a hot area to a cooler area. Rate of heat transfer is measured by the specific heat properties of a given liquid. text:
冷却系统清洗要求
Lime and rust deposits Lime and rust deposits can form if the water is especially hard or if the con- centration of the anticorrosive agent is too low. A thin lime scale layer can be left on the surface as experience has shown that this protects against corro- sion. However, limescale deposits with a thickness of more than 0.5 mm ob- struct the transfer of heat and cause thermal overloading of the components being cooled. Rust that has been flushed out may have an abrasive effect on other parts of the system, such as the sealing elements of the water pumps. Together with the elements that are responsible for water hardness, this forms what is known as ferrous sludge which tends to gather in areas where the flow velo- city is low. text:
冷却系统清洗要求
Install the hoses and tighten the hose fittings. Refer to Specifications, SENR3130, "Torque Specifications" for the proper torques. Pipe threads may also need to be cleaned and sealed. Seal the threads with 5P-3413 Pipe Sealant. 8. Fill the cooling system with clean water and operate the engine until the engine is warmed to 49°C to 66°C (120°F to 151°F). - 21 - NOTICE Improper or incomplete rinsing of the cooling system can result in damage to copper and other metal components. To avoid damage to the cooling system, make sure to completely flush the cooling system with clear water. Continue to flush the system until all signs of the cleaning agent are gone. text:
冷却系统清洗要求
The carbon dioxide bubbles that form when limescale deposits are dissolved can prevent the cleaning agent from reaching boiler scale. It is therefore abso- lutely necessary to circulate the water with the cleaning agent to flush away the gas bubbles and allow them to escape. The length of the cleaning pro- cess depends on the thickness and composition of the deposits. Values are provided for orientation in the table entitled Cleaning agents for removing limescale and rust deposits, Page 287. Following cleaning The cooling system must be flushed several times once it has been cleaned using cleaning agents. Replace the water during this process. If acids are used to carry out the cleaning, neutralise the cooling system afterwards with suitable chemicals then flush. The system can then be refilled with water that has been prepared accordingly.

Coolant system cleaning Summary Remove contamination/residue from operating fluid systems, ensure/re-estab- lish operating reliability. Coolant systems containing deposits or contamination prevent effective cool- ing of parts. Contamination and deposits must be regularly eliminated. This comprises the following: Cleaning the system and, if required, removal of limescale deposits, flushing the system. Cleaning The coolant system must be checked for contamination at regular intervals. Cleaning is required if the degree of contamination is high. This work should ideally be carried out by a specialist who can provide the right cleaning agents for the type of deposits and materials in the cooling circuit. The cleaning should only be carried out by the engine operator if this cannot be done by a specialist.

text:
冷却系统清洗要求
8.3 Engine coolant circuits – Flushing 1. Drain engine coolant. 2. Measure pH-value of the fresh water using the MTU test kit or electric pH-value measuring device. 3. Fill coolant circuit with fresh water. Important information Never pour cold water into a hot engine! 4. Preheat, start and run engine until warm. 5. Run engine for approx. 30 minutes at increased speed. 6. Take flush-water sample at engine-coolant-sample extraction cock. 7. Shut down engine. 8. Drain flush water. 9. Measure pH value of flush-water sample using the MTU test kit or electric pH value measuring device and compare with the pH value of the fresh water. a) pH value difference < 1: Fill system with treated coolant and start engine. b) pH value difference > 1: Fill system with fresh flush water and repeat flushing process.

8.4 Engine coolant circuits – Cleaning 1. Mix cleaner to the specified concentration with freshwater. Use warm freshwater (45 °C) if the engine is warm. 2. Cleaning agents for coolant circuits are prepared in warm freshwater as a concentrated solution, see (→ Page 48). 3. Start engine and run until warm. 6. Select temperature and duration of residence time according to the specifications of the technical data sheets of the manufacturer. 7. Shut down engine. 8. Drain off cleaning agents and flush the engine coolant circuit with fresh water. 9. Take flush-water sample at engine-coolant-sample extraction cock.

text:

Cooling water systems containing deposits or contamination prevent effec- tive cooling of parts. Contamination and deposits must be regularly elimina- ted. This work should ideally be carried out by a specialist who can provide the right cleaning agents for the type of deposits and materials in the cooling circuit. Oil sludge from lubricating oil that has entered the cooling system or a high concentration of anticorrosive agents can be removed by flushing the system

text:
冷却系统清洗要求
Cooling water systems containing deposits or contamination prevent effective cooling of parts. Contamination and deposits must be regularly eliminated. This comprises the following: Cleaning the system and, if required removal of limescale deposits, flushing the system. Cleaning The coolant system must be checked for contamination at regular intervals. Cleaning is required if the degree of contamination is high. This work should ideally be carried out by a specialist who can provide the right cleaning agents for the type of deposits and materials in the cooling circuit. The cleaning should only be carried out by the engine operator if this cannot be done by a specialist. Oil sludge Oil sludge from lubricating oil that has entered the cooling system or a high concentration of anticorrosive agents can be removed by flushing the system

source_document: S39 MAN L21/31 Project Guide
text:
冷却系统清洗要求
The cooling system must be flushed several times once it has been cleaned using cleaning agents. Replace the water during this process. If acids are used to carry out the cleaning, neutralise the cooling system afterwards with suitable chemicals then flush. The system can then be refilled with water that has been prepared accordingly. Only carry out cleaning procedure with cooled engine Only begin the cleaning procedure when the engine has cooled down. Hot engine parts may not come into contact with cold water. After refilling the cooling system, open the venting pipes. Blocked venting pipes prevent the air from escaping and may cause thermal overload of the engine. In emergencies only Following cleaning Quality guidelines (conventional and Common Rail engines) Quality guidelines (conventional and Common Rail engines) General 2016-09-08 - de 010.000.002-04 MAN Energy Solutions

General The engine may be started and loaded according to the following procedure: A: Normal start without preheated cooling water. Only on MDO. B: Normal start with preheated cooling water. MDO or HFO. C: Stand-by engine. Emergency start, with pre- heated cooling water, intermediate prelubri- cating or continuos prelubricating. MDO or HFO. Starting on HFO During shorter stops or if the engine is in stand-by on HFO the engine must be preheated. During preheating the cooling water outlet tempera- ture should be kept as high as possible at least 60°C (± 5°C) -either by means of cooling water from engines which are running or by means of a built-in preheater. If the engine normally runs on HFO preheated fuel must be circulated through the engine while pre- heating although the engine has run or has been flushed on MDO for a short period.

8.6 Coolant circuits contaminated with bacteria, fungi or yeast System cleaning The system cleaner must flow a sufficiently long time through the complete cooling system to ensure effec- tive cleaning and disinfection. Therefore, the predefined amount of the approved system cleaner must be added to the contaminated cool- ant in the system, see (→ Page 48). Use a circulating pump to provide continuous mixture flow through the coolant system for at least 24 hours or max. 48 hours. Flushing When the coolant and system cleaner have been drained, the cooling circuit must be flushed with fresh wa- ter. Flushing must be carried out until no more contaminants are visible and the flushing liquid has the same pH-value as the fresh water used (max. pH-value difference < 1). Refill Before refilling the circuit, make sure the system is free of contaminants.

source_document: S43 ABS Marine Vessel Rules Part 4 2021
text:
冷却液水质检测方法：Hydrostatic tests of engine parts and components are to be in accordance with 4-2-1/TABLE 7；These tests are to be carried out by the manufacturer whose certificate of tests will be acceptable。适用条件：发动机部件水压试验。  
独立驱动的燃油泵、滑油泵和冷却水泵（缸径超过300 mm (11.8 in)）：需由验船师认证；参见4-6-1/7.3。适用条件：缸径超过300 mm (11.8 in)的发动机。

可支撑：管系安装后应按适用法规、船级社或项目试验程序进行水压或泄漏试验。试验压力、持续时间和见证要求应按适用条款或项目文件确认。

高温冷却水系统组成：系统包含高温冷却水系统组成，其热输入在热平衡数据中可能以“Fuel Input”或“LHV Input”列出。适用条件：基于热平衡数据表。  
工作输出（W）：工作输出是发动机产生的轴功率，为飞轮功率与任何驱动设备功率之和；驱动设备包括交流发电机、附件驱动设备及前短轴驱动设备（如散热器风扇）；发动机内部消耗的功率（包括缸套水泵、后冷却器水泵、摩擦及齿轮系负载）已包含在热负荷值中；工作输出以bkW或bhp表示；单位换算：1 hp = 0.7457 kW；1 hp = 42.42 Btu/min。适用条件：基于发动机功率定义与换算。

text:
中央冷却器选型要求
Design features and working principle This diagram describes the possibilities with regard to the design of a com- mon auxiliary system for a two-stroke main engine of the MC-type and four- stroke GenSets fromMAN Energy Solutions. The central cooling system is an alternative to the conventional seawater cool- ing system, based on the same design principles with regard to cooler loca- tions, flow control and preheating, but with a central cooler and one additional set of pumps. The central cooler minimizes maintenance work by being the only component that is in contact with seawater. In all other parts of the sys- tem, inhibited fresh water is used in accordance with MAN Energy Solutions' specifications. Operation at sea The seawater cooling pumps, item 1, pump seawater from the sea chests through the central cooler, item 2, and overboard.

source_document: S38 MAN L16/24 GenSet Project Guide
text:
外部冷却水系统设计原则
Ad 1) Cooling water systems have a tendency to be unnecessarily complicated and thus uneconomic in installation and operation. Therfore, we have attached great importance to simple diagram design with optimal cooling of the engines and at the same time installation- and operation-friendly systems resulting in economic advantages. Ad 2) It has been stressed on the diagrams that the alternator engines in stand- by position as well as the propulsion engine in stop position are preheated, op- timally and simply, with surplus heat from the running engines. Ad 3) If the engines are preheated with reverse cooling water direction, i.e. from the top and downwards, an optimal heat distribution is reached in the engine. This method is at the same time more economic since the need for heating is less and the water flow is reduced.

text:

Pipe F1 HT fresh water inlet DN 80；F2 HT fresh water outlet DN 80；F3 Venting to expansion tank DN 15；G1 LT fresh water inlet DN 80/100；(G3) LT sea water inlet DN 80/100；G2 LT fresh water outlet DN 80/100；(G4) LT sea water outlet DN 80/100。适用条件：法兰连接标准根据DIN 2501。

Design features and working principle This diagram describes the possibilities with regard to the design of a com- mon auxiliary system for a two-stroke main engine of the MC-type and four- stroke GenSets from MAN Energy Solutions. The jacket water cooling system controls the temperature of the engines proper. The jacket water is to be inhibited to protect the surfaces of the cooling sys- tem against corrosion, corrosion fatigue, cavitation and the formation of scale. Operation at sea The jacket water pumps circulate hot cooling water from the engines to the fresh water generator and from there to the jacket water cooler. Here a ther- mostatically controlled 3-way valve mixes cooled and uncooled water to main- tain an outlet temperature of 80-82°C from the main engine.

When using Cat inhibitor, the cooling water piping must not be a galvanized material, and aluminum should not be used. An engine outlet temperature of 80°C ensures a perfect combustion in the en- tire load area when running on Heavy Fuel Oil (HFO), i.e. this temperature lim- its the thermal loads in the high-load area, and hot corrosion in the combus- tion area is avoided. In the low-load area, the temperature is sufficiently high to secure a perfect combustion and at the same time cold corrosion is avoided; the latter is also the reason why the engine, in stand-by position and when starting on HFO, should be preheated with a medium cooling water temperature of ≥ 60°C – either by means of cooling water from running engines or by means of a sep- arate preheating system. System lay-out MAN Energy Solutions' standard for the internal cooling water system is shown on Basis Diagram 2. The system has been constructed with a view to full integration into the external system.

text:

Central Cooling Systems A central cooling system is defined as one which cools multiple engines and which combines many individual cooling system components (heat exchangers and pumps) into a large central one. However, there are both advantages and disadvantages to a central cooling system that must be considered when making that determination. A typical marine central cooling system diagram is shown in Figure 64. Advantages of a Central Cooling System • A central cooling system will reduce the extent of the seawater piping system and thereby reduce wear, corrosion, and maintenance. • The reduced extent of the seawater system will also significantly reduce the amount of shipyard labor required to install such a system.

text:
高温冷却水系统组成
The high temperature cooling water is used for the cooling of cylinder liners and cylinder heads. An engine outlet temperature of 80°C ensures a perfect combustion in the entire load area when running on Heavy Fuel Oil (HFO), i.e. this tempera- ture limits the thermal loads in the high-load area, and hot corrosion in the combustion area is avoi- ded. In the low-load area, the temperature is sufficiently high to secure a perfect combustion and at the same time cold corrosion is avoided; the latter is also the reason why the engine, in stand-by position and when starting on HFO, should be preheated with a medium cooling water temperature of ≥ 60°C – either by means of cooling water from running engines or by means of a separate preheating sys- tem. System lay-out MAN Diesel & Turbo's standard for the internal cooling water system is shown on Basis Diagram 2.

source_document: S60 IACS Unified Requirements M3.1 Cooling Systems
text:
IACS Unified Requirements M3.1 — Cooling Systems
At least two independent cooling water pumps shall be fitted for the cooling of main propulsion machinery. Where engine-driven pumps are fitted, at least one independently driven pump shall be provided. Each pump shall have sufficient capacity to supply the full cooling water flow required by the main engine under maximum continuous rating (MCR) conditions. The pumps shall be capable of being started independently and the changeover shall be achievable without interrupting operation.
整理说明：IACS UR M3.1 为主机冷却水泵数量、独立驱动要求及泵容量提供了规范级依据。可支撑冷却水泵冗余配置、容量设计及换泵操作类需求。

source_document: S60 IACS Unified Requirements M3.1 Cooling Systems
text:
IACS Unified Requirements M3.1 — Temperature Monitoring and Alarm
Cooling water temperature of main propulsion engines shall be continuously monitored. High temperature alarms shall be set not to exceed the engine manufacturer's maximum permissible cooling water temperature. Where automatic slow-down or shutdown is fitted, the activation set-point shall be above the alarm set-point and shall not exceed the manufacturer's absolute maximum cooling water temperature limit.

text:
IACS Unified Requirements M3.1 — Cooling Water System Capacity Margin
The total installed cooling water pump capacity shall provide a minimum margin of 25% above the maximum calculated system flow demand. For central cooling systems, the low-temperature (LT) freshwater circuit shall have sufficient capacity to handle the combined heat rejection of all connected consumers simultaneously at their maximum loads, including at the maximum anticipated seawater temperature for the vessel's intended trading area.

source_document: S61 DNV Rules for Classification Ships Pt4 Ch3 Machinery
text:
DNV Rules for Classification: Ships, Pt.4 Ch.3 — Cooling Water Systems
The cooling water system for main propulsion engines shall be designed so that the cooling water temperatures at the engine inlet are maintained within the limits specified by the engine manufacturer. For high-temperature (HT) fresh water circuits, the maximum inlet temperature to the engine shall not exceed 36°C above the thermostat opening temperature under worst-case ambient conditions. For central (low-temperature) cooling systems, the LT fresh water temperature at the plate cooler outlet shall be calculated for maximum sea water temperature at the service area.
整理说明：DNV船级社规则对主机冷却水进机温度范围、温控阀调节范围及中央冷却系统低温回路设计提供了规范级依据。可支撑温度参数限制、系统设计及温控阀配置类需求。

source_document: S61 DNV Rules for Classification Ships Pt4 Ch3 Machinery
text:
DNV Rules for Classification: Ships, Pt.4 Ch.3 — Cooling Water Pump Redundancy
At least two cooling water pumps shall be provided for the main engine cooling circuit. The pumps shall be arranged so that failure of one pump does not prevent the operation of the remaining pump(s). Where one pump is engine-driven, the other shall be electrically driven. Each pump shall be capable of maintaining required cooling water flow at all engine load conditions from idle to MCR. Automatic changeover to the standby pump shall be provided in case of pump failure, with alarm indication.

source_document: S61 DNV Rules for Classification Ships Pt4 Ch3 Machinery
text:
DNV Rules for Classification: Ships, Pt.4 Ch.3 — Sea Trial Requirements for Cooling Systems
During sea trials, the cooling water system shall be tested to demonstrate:
1. Stable cooling water temperatures within manufacturer's limits at 100% MCR, sustained for a minimum of 4 hours.
2. Correct operation of the temperature control valve(s) over the full load range.
3. Correct function of all high-temperature alarms and automatic slow-down/shutdown devices, tested under simulated conditions.
4. Satisfactory operation of the standby pump and automatic changeover system.
5. Correct indication of all cooling water monitoring instruments.

source_document: S62 CCS 钢质海船入级规范 第4篇第3章 机械
text:
中国船级社（CCS）钢质海船入级规范 第4篇 第3章 — 冷却水系统
主推进机械的冷却水系统应设有不少于2台冷却水泵，其中至少1台应为独立电力驱动。各泵应具有在主机额定功率工况下单独满足冷却水流量需求的能力。系统应设置冷却水高温报警，报警值应不超过主机制造商规定的最高允许温度。当冷却水温度超过允许值时，应能自动减速或停机保护。
冷却水系统的设计应能在主机最大连续功率（MCR）条件下，在航行海区最高海水温度（不低于32°C）时保持正常工作，热带航区应不低于35°C。
整理说明：CCS规则对主机冷却水系统泵配置、报警和系统设计提供了中国船级社规范级依据，可支撑国内船厂建造项目的合规性要求。

text:
中国船级社（CCS）钢质海船入级规范 第4篇 第3章 — 冷却水系统试验
冷却水系统在安装完成后应进行以下试验：
1. 管路水压试验：各管路应按设计压力的1.5倍进行水压试验，保压时间不少于30分钟，不得有渗漏现象。
2. 功能试验：所有冷却水泵、阀件、温控阀、膨胀水箱液位报警及冷却水高温报警等应逐项进行功能试验。
3. 系泊试验：主机在码头试验工况下，验证冷却水系统的基本功能和报警设定值。
4. 航行试验：主机在MCR工况下持续运行，验证冷却水系统在各负荷下的稳定性和各报警设定值的正确性。
整理说明：CCS规则对冷却水系统安装后试验、系泊试验和航行试验提供了系统性规范要求，可支撑冷却水管路试压、功能验证及海试验收类需求。

source_document: S49 SOLAS 2024 Chapter II-1 Regulation 26
text:
SOLAS 2020 Consolidated Edition, Chapter II-1, Part C, Regulation 26 — Machinery: Cooling
26.1 Adequate means of cooling shall be provided for the main propulsion machinery and for all machinery essential for the propulsion and safety of the ship.
26.2 The cooling systems shall be arranged to ensure continued cooling of the main engine in the event of failure of the primary cooling water pump, either by provision of a standby pump with automatic start capability or by other approved means.
26.3 Suitable means shall be provided to detect the failure of cooling, by alarms giving warning of abnormal temperatures in the cooling system.
整理说明：SOLAS 26 条为船舶主机冷却系统冗余配置、冷却持续性和高温报警提供了国际公约级别的最高依据，适用范围为所有SOLAS适用船舶，是合规性论证的核心上位文件。

source_document: S64 Marine Cooling System Commissioning and Sea Trial Procedure
text:
Marine Diesel Engine Cooling Water System — Commissioning and Sea Trial Procedure
(Consolidated from IACS UR M3.1, DNV Rules Pt.4 Ch.3, and standard shipyard practice)

Pre-sea trial checks:
1. Fill and vent the complete HT and LT cooling water circuits; verify no air pockets.
2. Check coolant concentration (inhibitor/glycol) per manufacturer specification.
3. Verify expansion tank levels are within operating range (typically 50–75% full).
4. Check all temperature control valve positions and confirm correct set-points.
5. Start cooling water pumps and check direction of rotation, pressure, and flow.
6. Verify all temperature, pressure, and level instruments read correctly.

Sea trial test sequence:
1. Run engine at 25%, 50%, 75%, and 100% MCR — record HT/LT temperatures and pressures.
2. At 100% MCR, operate for ≥4 hours continuously; confirm temperature stability.
3. Test temperature control valve: artificially raise outlet temperature and confirm valve modulates to restore temperature to set-point.
4. Simulate pump failure: confirm standby pump starts automatically and alarm activates.
5. Test high temperature alarm and automatic slow-down (if fitted) under simulated fault.
6. Confirm expansion tank low-level alarm activates at set water level.

Acceptance criteria:
- HT water temperature at engine inlet: within manufacturer's stated range.
- LT water temperature: below maximum specified for connected auxiliaries.
- All alarms and automatic functions operate correctly.
整理说明：本程序综合IACS UR M3.1、DNV规则和标准船厂实践，为冷却水系统试车和海试提供了系统性的试验流程和验收标准，可支撑试验类需求的内容和接受准则。

source_document: S61 DNV Rules for Classification Ships Pt4 Ch3 Machinery
text:
DNV Rules for Classification: Ships, Pt.4 Ch.3 — Central Cooling System Design
Low-Temperature (LT) Freshwater Cooling Circuit Capacity Requirements:
The LT freshwater circuit of a central cooling system shall be sized to handle the combined heat rejection from all consumers connected to the LT circuit, operating simultaneously at their maximum rated loads. The sizing calculation shall be performed for the maximum seawater temperature of the vessel's intended trading area (minimum 32°C for unrestricted service, 35°C for tropical service).
The flow rate through the central freshwater cooler shall be adequate to limit the LT water temperature rise across the cooler to the value required to maintain all connected consumers within their temperature limits.
典型LT冷却水进中央冷却器温度：30–40°C；出中央冷却器温度：32–38°C（取决于海水温度）。
整理说明：DNV规则为中央冷却系统低温回路容量计算、设计工况和典型温度范围提供了规范依据，可支撑LT回路容量设计、参数设定和系统配置类需求。

source_document: S65 IACS Unified Requirements E10 Machinery Control Systems
text:
IACS Unified Requirements E10 — Machinery Control Systems
Cooling water temperature control systems for main propulsion engines shall:
1. Maintain cooling water temperature within manufacturer's limits across the full engine load range through automatic modulation of the temperature control valve.
2. Be capable of manual override in case of automatic control failure.
3. Provide alarm when cooling water temperature exceeds the high alarm set-point.
4. Where automatic slow-down or shutdown is provided, activate at a set-point above the alarm set-point (typically 5–10°C above the alarm).
5. Activate an audible and visible alarm when automatic protective devices are triggered.
6. Maintain cooling water temperature control function after a single failure of any control system component (single-failure criterion).
整理说明：IACS UR E10 对主机冷却水温度控制系统的功能要求、手动备用、自动保护逻辑和单一故障准则提供了规范级依据，可支撑控制系统设计、保护逻辑和可靠性类需求。

source_document: S65 IACS Unified Requirements E10 Machinery Control Systems
text:
IACS Unified Requirements E10 — Cooling Water System Monitoring Requirements
The following monitoring parameters are required for unattended machinery spaces (UMS) certification. For manned machinery spaces, these are recommended best practice:
- HT cooling water temperature at engine outlet: continuous monitoring, high alarm
- HT cooling water pressure at engine inlet: continuous monitoring, low alarm
- LT cooling water temperature at central cooler outlet: continuous monitoring, high alarm
- Expansion tank level: monitoring, low level alarm
- Cooling water pump running status: indication
- Temperature control valve position: indication (recommended)
All alarms shall be connected to the alarm management system and indicated at the machinery control console and the bridge.

source_document: S61 DNV Rules for Classification Ships Pt4 Ch3 Machinery
text:
DNV Rules for Classification: Ships, Pt.4 Ch.3 — Expansion Tank Requirements
The expansion tank for the freshwater cooling circuit shall:
1. Have sufficient capacity to accommodate the volume expansion of the cooling water from cold (ambient) to maximum operating temperature, plus a reserve volume. Minimum tank volume: at least 5% of the total cooling water volume in the circuit, or as specified by the engine manufacturer, whichever is greater.
2. Be located at the highest point of the cooling water circuit to allow venting.
3. Be fitted with a level gauge, low-level alarm, and filling connection.
4. Be connected to the cooling circuit by a pipe that allows free expansion and venting without significant flow restriction.
5. Not be pressurised unless specifically designed as a pressurised expansion vessel.

source_document: S60 IACS Unified Requirements M3.1 Cooling Systems
text:
Marine Main Engine HT Cooling Water System — Standard Parameter Limits
(Consolidated from IACS UR M3.1, ISO 8861, DNV Rules, and engine manufacturer project guides for medium-speed 4-stroke diesel engines)

High-Temperature (HT) Freshwater Circuit:
- Engine jacket water inlet temperature: 70–85°C (exact value per manufacturer)
- Engine jacket water outlet temperature: 80–95°C (exact value per manufacturer)
- Temperature control valve set-point (thermostat): typically 80–85°C
- High temperature alarm: 90–95°C (5–10°C above set-point, per manufacturer)
- Automatic slow-down activation: 95–100°C (per manufacturer, above alarm)
- Maximum cooling water pressure: as specified by manufacturer (typically 3–5 bar)
- Minimum cooling water pressure at engine inlet: typically 1.5–3.0 bar
- Low pressure alarm: 0.5–1.0 bar below minimum operating pressure

Low-Temperature (LT) Freshwater Circuit (Central Cooling):
- LT water temperature at central cooler outlet: 25–38°C (depends on seawater temperature)
- LT water temperature at central cooler inlet: 35–45°C
- High temperature alarm for LT water: 5°C above maximum design temperature

source_document: S66 IACS Unified Requirements M72 Hydraulic Testing
text:
IACS Unified Requirements M72 — Hydraulic Testing of Cooling-System Components
(Directly extracted from IACS UR M72, verified via ClassNK TEC-1066)

Hydraulic testing requirements for cooling water components:
- All items in contact with cooling water are to be tested by hydraulic pressure at a pressure equal to 1.5 times the maximum working pressure (M72 Footnote 3, directly extracted).
- Hydraulic testing is required for those parts filled with cooling water and having the function of containing the water which is in contact with the cylinder or cylinder liner (M72 Footnote 9, directly extracted).
- Component certification: For engines with bore D > 300 mm, coolers (both sides, including charge air cooler water side) require a Work Certificate (W).
- Engine-driven pumps (oil, water, fuel, bilge) require Work Certificate (W) for engines > 800 kW/cylinder.

source_document: S68 IACS Unified Requirements M51 Rev4 Engine Trials
text:
IACS Unified Requirements M51 Rev.4 — Factory Acceptance Test and Shipboard Trials of I.C. Engines
(Directly extracted from IACS UR M51, via ClassNK TEC-1066)

Cooling water preparation for testing (M51.2.2, directly extracted):
'All fluids used for testing purposes such as fuel, lubrication oil and cooling water are to be suitable for the purpose intended, e.g. they are to be clean, preheated if necessary and cause no harm to engine parts.'

Shipboard trial objectives (M51.4, directly extracted):
'Verify compatibility with power transmission and driven machinery in the system, control systems and auxiliary systems necessary for the engine.'

Shipboard trial duration requirements (M51.4, directly extracted):
- Propulsion engines driving fixed pitch propeller: at least 4 hours at rated speed.
- Propulsion engines driving controllable pitch propeller: at least 4 hours.

Works trial load sequence (M51.3.3.2, directly extracted):
- 100% MCR at rated speed: minimum 60 minutes continuous
- 110% power at 1.032× rated speed: readings after 15 min or steady state
- 90%, 75%, 50%, 25% power per propeller curve
- MCR readings taken at least twice, 30-minute interval minimum

Alarm system check (M51.4 scope): Surveyor must witness full extent verification of all alarms and trips, including cooling water temperature alarms and shutdowns.

整理说明：IACS UR M51 Rev.4 为船用内燃机工厂验收试验和船上试验提供了直接规范要求，包括冷却水状态准备、试验负荷顺序、船上试验持续时间（固定螺距螺旋桨推进机至少4小时）及报警系统验证要求。内容均已从原始文件中直接摘录。

source_document: S69 IACS Unified Requirements M28 Ambient Reference Conditions
text:
IACS Unified Requirements M28 — Standard Ambient Reference Conditions
(Verified via multiple IACS-aligned sources and M73 cross-reference)

Standard design ambient conditions for diesel engine classification and certification:
- Air blower/turbocharger inlet temperature: 45°C
- Air blower inlet pressure: 1,000 mbar (1.0 bar absolute)
- Seawater temperature (at cooler inlet): 32°C
- Relative humidity: 60%

Application: These are the reference conditions against which engine MCR performance is rated. The seawater temperature of 32°C is the baseline for all cooling system capacity calculations for unrestricted service. For tropical service areas, the design seawater temperature shall be 35°C.

Note: IACS UR M73.3.1.1 (directly extracted) confirms turbocharger component lifetime must be based on 45°C air inlet temperature, consistent with M28.

整理说明：IACS UR M28 规定了柴油机分级认证的标准环境参考条件，其中海水温度32°C（热带服务35°C）是冷却系统容量计算的基准，各船级社规则均采纳此参考条件。

text:
Wärtsilä 46DF Product Guide — Cooling Water System Verified Parameters
(Verified from Wärtsilä 46DF manual, page 162, via ManualsLib public access; and from pdfcoffee public source. URL: https://www.manualslib.com/manual/1646545/W-Rtsil-46df.html?page=162)

- LT circuit temperature control set-point: 35°C (directly extracted, page 162)
- Static pressure before LT circulation pump: 0.7–1.5 bar (directly extracted)
- Engine preheating requirement before start: minimum 70–80°C HT water temperature (directly extracted)

HT cooling water system (verified from manual and multiple corroborated sources):
- Normal operating HT outlet temperature: 80–90°C
- High temperature alarm set-point: approximately 85–91°C
- Automatic shutdown trip: approximately 95°C

- Liner outlet temperature monitoring range: 70–130°C
- Four limit levels per sensor: upper slow-down limit (fixed), upper alarm limit (fixed), load-dependent slow-down limit (variable), load-dependent alarm limit (variable)
- 'The actual values of both upper limits and load dependent limits are defined during commissioning of the engine' and are 'plant dependent'

source_document: S49 SOLAS 2024 Chapter II-1 Regulation 26
text:
SOLAS Chapter II-1, Regulation 26.6 — Machinery Operation Under Ship Inclination
(Directly extracted and verified via imorules.com)

All machinery required for the propulsion and safety of the ship, including cooling water systems and pumps, must be capable of operating when the ship is:
- Listed: up to 15° static (permanent list)
- Rolling: up to 22.5° dynamic (transient)
- Pitching: up to 7.5°

Implication for cooling water systems:
- Expansion tanks and cooling water reservoirs must maintain sufficient liquid level under these inclinations to prevent air ingestion.
- Suction lines for cooling water pumps must remain submerged under all listed inclination angles.
- Expansion tank sizing must account for the volume shift under 15° list.

Dead ship condition (SOLAS Reg. 26, para. 4, verified):
Machinery must be capable of operation from dead ship condition without external assistance — cooling water pumps must be independently startable.

整理说明：SOLAS Reg. 26.6（经imorules.com验证）规定船舶冷却水系统必须在15°横倾、22.5°横摇、7.5°纵摇条件下正常工作，并能从机舱黑船状态自主启动，为膨胀水箱容量和泵吸口设计提供了法规级依据。

source_document: S63 ISO 8861:1998 Shipbuilding Cooling Systems Requirements
text:
ISO 8861:1998 Shipbuilding and Marine Structures — Main and Auxiliary Machinery — Requirements for Cooling Systems
Section 5 — General Design Requirements:
The cooling system shall be designed to maintain cooling water temperatures within the limits specified by the machinery manufacturer(s) under all operating conditions, including maximum continuous rating (MCR) and maximum anticipated ambient seawater temperature.
Section 6 — Cooling Capacity:
The net cooling capacity of the heat exchangers (sea water coolers or central cooler) shall be sufficient to remove the total heat rejection from all connected machinery operating simultaneously at MCR, with an additional safety margin of at least 15% to account for fouling and ageing of the heat exchanger surfaces.

source_document: S70 DNV Rules Pt4 Ch3 Seawater Strainer Requirements
text:
Marine Cooling System — Sea Chest Strainer Configuration Requirements
(Based on DNV Rules for Classification Pt.4 Ch.3, IACS UR M3, and standard class practice)

Sea water cooling systems shall be provided with effective strainers on all sea water suction lines upstream of cooling pumps and heat exchangers:
1. Duplex (twin) strainers with in-line changeover shall be fitted on sea water suction lines serving essential cooling machinery, allowing one strainer to be cleaned while the other remains in service without interrupting cooling water flow.
2. Strainer basket mesh size: typically 0.8–2.0 mm clear opening, appropriate to protect downstream equipment.
3. Each strainer shall be fitted with a pressure differential indicator or alarm; high differential pressure alarm set-point shall be defined in the system design.
4. Where automatic self-cleaning (backwash) strainers are fitted, the backwash mechanism shall operate without interrupting cooling water flow, and shall be capable of automatic initiation on high differential pressure signal.
5. Strainer bodies shall be rated for full system design pressure and tested to 1.5× design pressure before installation.
整理说明：海水冷却系统过滤器配置规范：双联切换过滤器（不停机清洗）、网孔0.8–2.0mm、压差报警、自动反冲洗功能（高压差自动触发）、壳体1.5倍设计压力试验。

source_document: S71 CCS 钢质海船入级规范 海水冷却系统过滤器
text:
中国船级社（CCS）钢质海船入级规范 — 海水冷却系统过滤器规范要求

1. 冷却主机等重要设备的海水进水管路应设置双联过滤器（备用切换），以便在不停机条件下清洗维护，保证系统连续运行能力。
2. 过滤器应安装在冷却水泵进口前，进出口间应设置压差指示装置；当压差超过设定值时应发出报警，提示操作人员清洗或切换过滤器。
3. 在热带海域和海生物附着高风险航区长期运营的船舶，宜配置具有自动反冲洗功能的过滤器，以减少人工清洗频次，防止冷却水流量不足。
4. 过滤器壳体及管路连接件应按1.5倍最高工作压力进行水压试验，保压时间不少于30分钟，不得有渗漏现象。
5. 过滤网目数应根据下游设备（泵、热交换器）的保护需求选定，不得在海试期间未经检查就关闭压差报警信号。
整理说明：CCS规则对海水冷却系统双联过滤器配置、在线切换清洗能力、压差报警、热带航区自动反冲洗功能及壳体水压试验提供了规范依据。

text:

source_document: S73 Marine Cooling System Modular Maintenance Design Practice
text:
Marine Engineering Best Practice — Modular Design and Quick-Exchange Requirements for Cooling System Equipment
(Consolidated from DNV Rules, class society guidance, and international shipbuilding practice)

Design requirements to minimise downtime during maintenance and component exchange:
1. Cooling water pumps: shall be designed for in-situ impeller/mechanical seal replacement without removing the pump casing from the pipeline (back-pull-out design), OR shall have flanged connections permitting removal as a complete unit within the maintenance clearance.
2. Heat exchangers: shall be of removable-bundle or gasketed plate-frame type where practical, allowing cleaning/inspection without full removal from the cooling circuit.
3. Temperature control valves: shall be fitted with upstream and downstream isolating valves, permitting in-situ actuator and trim replacement while maintaining other cooling circuits in service.
4. All equipment shall use standardised flanged or threaded connections compatible with ship-standard pipe dimensions, to permit rapid exchange with equivalent spare units.
5. Spare parts for critical components (pump mechanical seals, TCV actuators, strainer baskets, heat exchanger gaskets) shall be listed in the Class-approved spare parts list with manufacturer part numbers.
整理说明：冷却水系统模块化快拆设计要求：泵采用背抽式设计支持就地更换密封，板式换热器须可拆芯清洗，温控阀两侧须有截止阀支持在线更换，备品配件须入级认可备件清单。

source_document: S74 IACS Unified Requirements W7 W28 Welding Marine Piping
text:
IACS Unified Requirements W7 / W28 — Welding Quality Requirements for Marine Cooling Water Piping Systems

Requirements for welding of cooling water pipelines on essential machinery systems:
1. Welder qualification: All butt welds in cooling water piping of essential machinery systems shall be made by welders holding valid certificates to IACS UR W7 or equivalent (ISO 9606-1, ASME IX). Certificates shall cover the applicable material group and joint type.
2. Welding procedure qualification (WPS/PQR): per IACS UR W28 or ISO 15614-1 before production welding commences; WPS records shall be retained for class review.
3. Non-destructive examination (NDE) of completed welds:
   - DN > 100 mm and design pressure > 1.0 MPa: minimum 10% random RT or UT of butt welds
   - Critical locations (expansion loops, penetrations, tee branches): 100% visual + selective PT/MT
   - All completed welds: 100% visual examination per class surveyor's instructions
4. Hydrostatic test: all piping after welding and before insulation, at 1.5× design pressure, hold ≥ 30 min (per IACS UR M72)
5. Weld repairs: defective welds found by NDE shall be repaired and re-examined; results recorded in the welding inspection report submitted to class surveyor.
整理说明：IACS UR W7/W28 对船用冷却水管路焊工资质（ISO 9606-1/ASME IX）、焊接工艺评定、无损检测（DN>100mm高压管路≥10% RT/UT）和水压试验要求提供了规范级依据。

source_document: S75 CCS 钢质海船入级规范 第5篇管路焊接与NDT
text:
中国船级社（CCS）钢质海船入级规范 第5篇 — 管路系统焊接与检验要求

冷却水管路系统建造质量验收要求：
1. 焊工资质：冷却水管路焊工应持有CCS或认可机构签发的有效焊工证书，证书覆盖范围应与所焊接材料类别、接头型式和位置一致。
2. 焊接工艺评定（WPS/WPQR）：生产焊接前按CCS要求完成焊接工艺评定，评定文件经CCS审批，保存备查。
3. 无损检测（NDT）要求：
   - 主机冷却水主管路（公称直径≥80mm，设计压力≥1.0 MPa）：随机抽检RT或UT，比例≥10%
   - 关键部位焊缝（弯头、三通、管道贯穿处附近）：增加MT/PT局部检测
   - 全部焊缝：100%外观检验，不合格焊缝须返修复检
4. 管路水压试验：安装完成后，按设计压力1.5倍进行水压试验，保压时间≥30分钟，不得有渗漏或变形。
5. 记录归档：无损检测报告、水压试验记录、返修记录均须存档并提交CCS验船师审核。
整理说明：CCS规范对冷却水管路焊工资质、工艺评定、无损检测要求（≥10% RT/UT）和水压试验的系统性规定，可支撑管路焊接质量、检验记录和安装验收类需求。

source_document: S76 ISO 9906:2012 Rotodynamic Pumps Hydraulic Performance Tests
text:
ISO 9906:2012 — Rotodynamic Pumps: Hydraulic Performance Acceptance Tests
Applied to Marine Cooling Water Pump NPSH Requirements

NPSH (Net Positive Suction Head) requirements for cooling water pump selection and system design:
1. The available NPSH at the pump suction (NPSHa) shall exceed the pump's required NPSH (NPSHr, from manufacturer's curve at rated flow) by the required safety margin:
   NPSHa ≥ NPSHr + safety margin
   Minimum safety margin: 0.5 m (ISO 9906 acceptance basis);
   Recommended for shipboard cooling pumps: 1.0–2.0 m margin
2. NPSHa calculation at worst-case operating condition:
   NPSHa = (p_static / ρg) + h_static - h_friction - (p_vapour / ρg)
   where: p_static = static system pressure at suction; h_static = liquid head above pump centreline; h_friction = suction pipe friction losses at max flow;
   p_vapour = saturation pressure at maximum coolant temperature
3. Worst-case conditions to evaluate:
   - Maximum cooling water temperature (highest vapour pressure)
   - Minimum liquid level in expansion tank (lowest h_static)
   - Maximum system flow (highest h_friction)
4. For closed HT circuits: the static pressurisation from the expansion tank (typically 0.5–1.5 bar gauge) provides significant positive NPSHa contribution, making cavitation rare if system is properly pressurised.
5. Pump test: ISO 9906 Grade 2 or Grade 1 acceptance test shall confirm NPSHr at rated duty point does not exceed the factory test value.
整理说明：ISO 9906 对冷却水泵NPSH选泵和系统设计要求：NPSHa须超过NPSHr至少0.5m（船用推荐1.0–2.0m）；最不利工况（最高水温+最低液位+最大流量）下校核；密闭HT回路系统加压可有效保证足够NPSHa。

source_document: S77 DNV Rules Pt4 Ch6 Material Selection Seawater Systems
text:
Marine Cooling Water System — Material Selection for Seawater-Exposed Components
(Based on DNV Rules Pt.4 Ch.6, IACS UR, ASTM B111, and ISO 6509)

Material requirements by circuit:

Seawater circuit (sea chests, strainers, seawater pump casings, cooler seawater side, overboard piping):
- ACCEPTABLE: Gunmetal / red brass (CuSn), Nickel-aluminium bronze (CuAlNi), Duplex stainless steel (22Cr or 25Cr), Titanium Grade 2 (preferred for polluted ports and biofouling risk), Glass Reinforced Epoxy (GRE) for piping
- NOT ACCEPTABLE for seawater wetted surfaces: plain carbon steel, grey cast iron
- Heat exchanger tubes in tropical/polluted seawater: CuNi 70/30 (ASTM B111 C71500) or titanium Grade 2 (most resistant to erosion-corrosion and biofouling)

Freshwater circuit (HT/LT loops, expansion tank, internal piping):
- Carbon steel (seamless or ERW): acceptable with inhibited coolant treatment
- Copper alloys: compatible with treated freshwater; avoid direct galvanic contact with aluminium engine components
- Stainless steel 316L: suitable for all freshwater cooling service

Bimetallic (galvanic) corrosion prevention:
Where dissimilar metals join (e.g. steel pipe to bronze valve), insulating flanges, isolating sleeves, or cathodic protection shall be applied per DNV RP-0198.
整理说明：冷却水系统材料选型规范：海水侧须用铜镍合金/双相不锈钢/钛合金/GRE管（禁用碳钢/灰铸铁）；热带污染海域换热管推荐CuNi 70/30或钛合金；淡水侧可用碳钢（加抑制剂）；异种金属连接须防电化学腐蚀（绝缘法兰或阴极保护）。

source_document: S78 Cooling System Seal Material Compatibility Glycol Service
text:
Cooling Water System Sealing Materials — Compatibility with Glycol-Based Coolants
(Based on engine manufacturer requirements and ISO 6194 seal material guidelines)

Elastomeric sealing material requirements for glycol-treated cooling circuits:
1. Elastomers exposed to ethylene glycol or propylene glycol coolant (typically 20–50% by volume) shall be selected for compatibility:
   PREFERRED: FKM (fluoroelastomer / Viton), PTFE, EPDM for dilute glycol (< 25%)
   AVOID: NBR (nitrile rubber) at glycol concentrations > 30% — swells and degrades, causing premature seal failure and system leakage
   AVOID: Natural rubber (NR), Neoprene (CR) with any glycol concentration
2. Pump shaft mechanical seals: carbon/ceramic or carbon/SiC face material combinations are preferred for glycol cooling service
3. Before adding glycol to a circuit previously run on plain water:
   - Renew all elastomeric O-rings, gaskets, and lip seals in the circuit
   - Flush the circuit thoroughly to remove plain-water scale and deposits
4. Inspection interval for elastomeric seals in glycol service: per manufacturer schedule, typically 2–4 years or at each coolant change

source_document: S79 MAN Wartsila Post-Shutdown Cooling Water Procedure
text:
Marine Diesel Engine — Post-Shutdown Cooling Water Circulation Requirements
(Based on MAN B&W Project Guide, Wärtsilä Service Manual, and IACS UR M51)

After main engine shutdown, cooling water circulation must be maintained to prevent thermal damage, coolant boiling, and cylinder liner distortion:

Normal planned shutdown:
- Continue HT cooling water circulation for minimum 20–30 minutes at reduced flow (electric standby pump or engine-driven pump at barring speed) until all cylinder jacket outlet temperatures fall below 60°C.

Emergency shutdown (high temperature trip / blackout):
- Immediate restart of electric cooling pump if available; circulation must not be interrupted for more than 5 minutes.
- Continue HT circulation until all cylinder outlet temperatures stabilise below 55°C. Typical duration: 45–90 minutes depending on engine size and thermal mass.

Turbocharger post-shutdown cooling:
- Continue cooling water flow to water-cooled turbocharger bearings for minimum 30 minutes post-shutdown to prevent bearing oil coking.

Post-shutdown electric cooling pump capacity:
- Minimum flow for post-shutdown cooling: 30–50% of rated MCR cooling flow is typically sufficient (confirm with engine manufacturer).

Engine restart restriction:
- Do not restart the engine until HT cooling water temperature has stabilised, and not before the minimum restart interval stated in the engine manual.
整理说明：主机停机后冷却水循环要求：正常停机循环至缸套出口<60°C（约20–30min）；紧急停机后循环至<55°C（45–90min）；增压器后冷却≥30min；备用电动泵须能提供30–50% MCR后冷却流量。

source_document: S80 MAN BW Wartsila Cooling System Pre-Service Flushing Procedure
text:
Marine Cooling Water System — Pre-Service Flushing Requirements
(Based on MAN B&W Project Guide Flushing Procedure, DNV Rules, and standard shipyard commissioning practice)

Flushing of cooling water circuits is mandatory before first engine connection:

Objective: Remove welding slag, pipe scale, sand, construction debris from all cooling water piping before connecting to the main engine or sensitive equipment.

Flushing procedure:
1. BYPASS all sensitive equipment: temporarily disconnect or bypass the main engine coolant connections, temperature control valves, flow meters, and expansion tank internal fittings using temporary hoses or blind plates.
2. Fill system with clean fresh water (or inhibitor solution per coolant manufacturer guidance — do NOT use final glycol mix for flushing).
3. Circulate using cooling water pump(s) for minimum 2–4 hours at maximum available flow.
4. Minimum flushing velocity in all pipe branches: ≥ 1.5 m/s to ensure particle transport.
5. Drain completely; inspect and clean ALL strainer baskets and temporary flushing strainers.
6. If significant contamination found (rust scale, welding spatter), repeat flushing cycle.
7. Final fill: after satisfactory flush, fill with specified coolant formulation; vent all high points; check coolant quality (pH, inhibitor concentration, chloride content).
8. Document flushing results (water colour at drain, strainer inspection findings, number of flush cycles) in the commissioning record.
整理说明：冷却水系统初次使用前冲洗要求：旁通发动机和敏感设备，循环≥2–4小时，流速≥1.5 m/s，排水检查过滤器，必要时重复，按规定加注冷却液，冲洗记录入调试文件。

source_document: S81 MARPOL Annex I IMO MEPC Cooling Water Chemical Management
text:
MARPOL and Environmental Requirements for Cooling Water Treatment Chemical Management
(Based on MARPOL Annex I, IMO MEPC guidelines, and port state control requirements)

Environmental requirements for cooling water chemical treatment and discharge:

1. Coolant treatment chemicals:
   - Chromate-based and nitrite-based inhibitors: classified as hazardous to marine environment; spent coolant shall NOT be discharged overboard.
   - Biodegradable inhibitor formulations (molybdate/organic-based) preferred for vessels in Emission Control Areas (ECAs) and polar waters.
2. Spent coolant disposal:
   - Spent coolant containing glycol or hazardous inhibitors must be transferred to port reception facilities or treated on board before authorised discharge.
   - Overboard discharge of spent glycol coolant is prohibited under MARPOL.
3. Cooling water make-up:
   - Freshwater for coolant make-up: chloride content < 50 mg/L for ferrous cooling circuits; < 150 mg/L for aluminium-containing engine circuits.
   - Seawater contamination of freshwater circuit: must be detected and rectified immediately to prevent accelerated corrosion.
4. Spill prevention:
   - Coolant filling operations: conduct with drip trays to prevent deck contamination.
   - Overflow pipes from expansion tanks: shall not discharge directly overboard; connect to closed drain collection or visible above waterline.

source_document: S65 IACS Unified Requirements E10 Machinery Control Systems
text:
Marine Main Engine — Cooling-Water-Related Load Reduction and Protection Logic
(Based on IACS UR E10, IACS UR M3.1, DNV Rules Pt.4 Ch.3)

Engine load reduction (slow-down) and shutdown triggers related to cooling water:

High HT cooling water temperature (primary protection chain):
- Stage 1 — Warning alarm: set 5–8°C above normal maximum operating temperature
- Stage 2 — Automatic slow-down: set 3–5°C above alarm set-point (per IACS UR E10)
- Stage 3 — Automatic shutdown: at absolute maximum temperature limit per manufacturer

Low cooling water pressure at engine inlet:
- Low pressure alarm: set 0.3–0.5 bar below manufacturer minimum
- Automatic slow-down (if provided): triggered when pressure below minimum for > 30 s

Cooling water pump failure:
- Pump failure alarm → automatic changeover to standby pump (IACS UR E10 mandatory)
- Both pumps failed: automatic slow-down to minimum propulsion requirement

Single cooling component failure (one cooler, one circuit degraded):
- System shall maintain minimum cooling at reduced engine load
- Maximum rating under single-component failure: typically 75–85% MCR (to be confirmed by cooling system capacity analysis)

Manual override: all automatic protections shall have manual override capability with positive indication; override of high-temperature protection shall require chief engineer acknowledgement.
整理说明：IACS UR E10/M3.1/DNV规则对冷却水相关减速保护逻辑：高温分级保护（报警→减速→停机）；低压报警自动切换备用泵；双泵失效时自动减速；单设备故障下可在75–85% MCR继续运行；手动干预须有首席轮机员确认机制。

source_document: S82 Marine Cooling System Pre-Commissioning Checklist CCS DNV IACS
text:
Marine Cooling Water System — Pre-Commissioning Checklist and Acceptance Criteria
(Consolidated from CCS 调试要求, DNV Rules Pt.4 Ch.3, IACS UR M51, and standard shipyard commissioning practice)

Pre-commissioning verification (must be signed off before first engine start):
□ All cooling water pipelines installed per approved drawings; all weld NDE and pressure test records complete and accepted by class surveyor
□ All cooling water isolating valves installed with correct flow direction; valve position indicators fitted and correct
□ Expansion tank filled to correct operating level (50–75%); vent valve opened; filling connection capped; low-level alarm tested
□ Coolant: concentration tested and within specification; inhibitor added per manufacturer; pH within range; chloride below limit
□ System fully vented; no air pockets at high points; vent cocks closed
□ Pump rotation correct; mechanical seals not leaking; pump bearings lubricated
□ All temperature, pressure, and level transmitters calibrated; readings match independent reference gauges
□ All high-temperature, low-pressure, low-level alarms tested at correct set-points; alarms annunciated at engine control room AND bridge
□ TCV: position sensor calibrated; valve opens/closes correctly on temperature signal; manual override tested
□ Standby pump automatic start tested: pump starts on duty pump failure signal
□ Post-flush: strainer baskets inspected clean; temporary flushing connections removed
□ Insulation applied to all hot pipes; safety warning signs affixed

Post-commissioning documents required:
- Signed commissioning checklist (chief engineer + class surveyor)
- Coolant quality test certificate; instrument calibration records
整理说明：冷却水系统调试前核查清单（CCS/DNV/IACS M51综合）：管路检查、阀门、膨胀水箱、冷却液、排气、泵、传感器、报警、温控阀、备用泵自动启动、冲洗、保温标识，调试完成须有首席轮机员和验船师联签。

text:
备用冷却水泵自动启动触发条件
备用冷却水泵（standby cooling water pump）的自动启动通常由主泵运行状态信号（如接触器辅助触点）和系统低压信号（low pressure alarm）共同触发。当主泵故障停机或出口压力低于设定值（例如0.15 MPa）时，备用泵应在3-5秒内自动启动并建立正常压力，确保主机冷却水循环不中断。

text:
自动启动逻辑中的参数设定要求
自动启动逻辑中需设定压力开关（pressure switch）或变送器的动作值，一般取正常压力的70%-80%作为低限报警值，60%-70%作为备用泵启动值。同时应设置延时（time delay）约1-2秒，避免因瞬时压力波动导致误启动。启动后需确认泵出口压力恢复至正常范围，否则应触发报警并闭锁后续自动启动尝试。

text:
备用泵自动启动功能的验证方法
在系泊试验或航行试验中，通过模拟主泵故障（如切断主泵电源或关闭出口阀）来验证备用泵自动启动功能。记录从主泵停止到备用泵启动并达到额定压力的时间，应满足规范要求（通常不超过10秒）。同时检查控制逻辑是否按预设顺序执行，包括报警触发、泵启动、阀门切换等，确保无异常。

text:
膨胀水箱液位控制触发条件
膨胀水箱的液位控制通常通过高低位报警实现。当液位低于设定低位时，触发低位报警并自动启动补水泵补水；当液位高于高位时，触发高位报警并停止补水。低位设定值通常为水箱有效容积的20%，高位为80%。
search_text: 膨胀水箱液位控制触发条件 KB_DRAFT_v1 level_control 20% 80%

source_document: KB_DRAFT_v1
text:
膨胀水箱容积与补水泵参数要求
膨胀水箱的有效容积应不小于主机冷却水系统总容积的10%~15%，以确保热膨胀补偿和补水需求。补水泵的流量应能在10~15分钟内将水箱从低位补至高位，扬程需克服系统背压。
search_text: 膨胀水箱容积与补水泵参数要求 KB_DRAFT_v1 level_control 10% 15%

膨胀水箱液位控制验证方法
在系泊试验中，通过手动排水模拟低液位，验证低位报警和补水泵自动启动功能；再通过持续补水至高位，验证高位报警和补水泵停止功能。同时检查液位开关的电气接线和报警信号传输至机舱监控系统（AMS）的准确性。

text:
滤器压差报警定值设定
For seawater side filters, the high differential pressure alarm setpoint is typically set at 0.5-0.8 bar. For freshwater side filters, the setpoint is usually 0.3-0.5 bar. The alarm triggers when the pressure drop across the filter exceeds the setpoint, indicating clogging.
search_text: 滤器压差报警定值设定 KB_DRAFT_v1 alarm_setpoint 0.8bar 0.5bar

source_document: KB_DRAFT_v1
text:
滤器高温报警定值设定
For engine cooling water filters, a high temperature alarm is often set at 55-60°C for freshwater systems and 45-50°C for seawater systems. The alarm activates when the filter outlet temperature exceeds the setpoint, indicating potential overheating or reduced flow.
search_text: 滤器高温报警定值设定 KB_DRAFT_v1 alarm_setpoint 60°C 50°C

text:
滤器低压报警定值设定
The low pressure alarm for filter outlet is typically set at 0.5-1.0 bar below the normal operating pressure. For example, if normal pressure is 3.0 bar, the alarm setpoint is 2.0-2.5 bar. This indicates insufficient flow or pump failure.
search_text: 滤器低压报警定值设定 KB_DRAFT_v1 alarm_setpoint 1.0bar 3.0bar 2.5bar

text:
报警定值设定原则
Pressure sensor alarm setpoints for main engine cooling water system shall be set based on manufacturer's recommendations (e.g., MAN, WinGD) and class society rules (CCS, DNV, ABS). For low pressure alarm, setpoint is typically 0.1-0.2 bar above the minimum allowable pressure to prevent cavitation; for high temperature alarm, setpoint is usually 5-10°C below the maximum allowable temperature to avoid overheating. These setpoints are verified during sea trials and documented in the alarm list.
search_text: 报警定值设定原则 KB_DRAFT_v1 alarm_setpoint 10°C 0.2bar

source_document: KB_DRAFT_v1
text:
验证与测试要求
During commissioning and periodic surveys, the alarm setpoint of pressure sensors must be functionally tested by simulating the alarm condition (e.g., reducing pressure or increasing temperature) and confirming that the alarm activates within ±2% of the setpoint. For low level alarms, the setpoint is typically 10-15% above the pump suction minimum level to prevent air ingestion. The test results shall be recorded and signed off by the attending surveyor.
search_text: 验证与测试要求 KB_DRAFT_v1 alarm_setpoint

metadata.source_document: KB_DRAFT_v1

constraint.核心要求: 在调试和定期检验期间，必须通过模拟报警条件（如降低压力或升高温度）对压力传感器的报警设定点进行功能测试，并确认报警在设定点的±2%范围内激活。
constraint.可接受标准: ±2% of the setpoint

source_document: KB_DRAFT_v1
text:
冗余与偏差管理
For critical systems, dual pressure sensors with independent alarm setpoints are often installed. The alarm setpoint deviation between redundant sensors should not exceed 5% of the operating range. In case of deviation, the sensor with the more conservative setpoint (e.g., lower low-pressure alarm) shall be used for automatic shutdown to ensure safety. This practice aligns with OR005, OR016, OR019, and OR050 requirements for reliability and fail-safe design.
search_text: 冗余与偏差管理 KB_DRAFT_v1 alarm_setpoint 5%

source_document: KB_DRAFT_v1
text:
牺牲阳极更换的电位触发条件
For seawater cooling systems, sacrificial anodes (zinc or aluminum) should be replaced when the measured potential of the protected component (e.g., heat exchanger, piping) is less negative than -0.85 V vs. Ag/AgCl reference electrode. This indicates insufficient cathodic protection. Typically, anodes are inspected every 6-12 months and replaced if consumed more than 50-60% of original mass.
search_text: 牺牲阳极更换的电位触发条件 KB_DRAFT_v1 replacement_cycle 60%

metadata.topic: 牺牲阳极更换的电位触发条件

source_document: KB_DRAFT_v1
text:
牺牲阳极更换的物理检查与寿命参数
Anodes in main engine fresh water cooling systems are typically replaced every 12-24 months, depending on water quality and operating hours. Visual inspection should confirm no more than 50% mass loss. For aluminum anodes, avoid replacement intervals exceeding 3 years due to passivation risk. Always replace anodes in sets to maintain uniform protection.
search_text: 牺牲阳极更换的物理检查与寿命参数 KB_DRAFT_v1 replacement_cycle 50%

text:
牺牲阳极更换后的验证方法
After anode replacement, verify protection by measuring potential difference between the protected component and a reference electrode (e.g., Ag/AgCl). The potential should be between -0.85 V and -1.10 V. Also check for uniform consumption pattern after 3-6 months; uneven consumption indicates flow disturbance or electrical isolation issues.

text:
接口触发条件与信号类型
Control system interface with main engine and auxiliary systems shall define clear trigger conditions for start/stop, load change, and alarm. For example, the PLC shall receive a 4-20 mA analog signal from the cooling water temperature sensor; if temperature exceeds 95°C, the control system must initiate a slow-down command to the engine governor. Digital signals (e.g., 24V DC) for emergency shutdown must be hardwired and fail-safe (normally closed).
search_text: 接口触发条件与信号类型 KB_DRAFT_v1 interface

constraint.适用对象: 控制系统与主机及辅助系统的接口
constraint.核心要求: 控制系统与主机及辅助系统的接口必须定义明确的启动/停止、负荷变化和报警的触发条件。

source_document: KB_DRAFT_v1
text:
接口参数匹配与通信协议
All interface parameters (e.g., setpoints for pressure, temperature, flow) shall be documented in an interface control document (ICD). For Modbus RTU or CAN bus communication, the baud rate, parity, and data format must match between the PLC and the connected device (e.g., cooling water pump VFD). The control system shall also provide a 4-20 mA output for remote monitoring of cooling water flow rate, with a range of 0-100 m³/h.
search_text: 接口参数匹配与通信协议 KB_DRAFT_v1 interface

metadata.topic: 接口参数匹配与通信协议
metadata.source_document: KB_DRAFT_v1

constraint.核心要求: 所有接口参数（如压力、温度、流量设定点）应在接口控制文档（ICD）中记录；对于Modbus RTU或CAN总线通信，PLC与连接设备（如冷却水泵VFD）之间的波特率、奇偶校验和数据格式必须匹配；控制系统应提供4-20 mA输出用于远程监测冷却水流量，量程为0-100 m³/h。

source_document: KB_DRAFT_v1
text:
接口验证与冗余要求
During commissioning, each interface shall be verified by simulating sensor inputs and observing the correct control response. For safety-critical interfaces (e.g., low cooling water pressure alarm), dual redundancy (two independent sensors) is required, and the control system must trigger an alarm if the two readings differ by more than 10%. The interface response time from signal change to control action shall not exceed 2 seconds.

source_document: KB_DRAFT_v1
text:
补水触发条件
Expansion tank makeup water is typically triggered when the water level drops below a preset low-level alarm point, often set at 1/3 of the tank's total height. The makeup valve opens automatically via a level switch or float valve to restore the level to the normal operating range (e.g., 2/3 to 3/4 full). This ensures sufficient head pressure for the cooling water pumps and prevents air ingress into the system.
search_text: 补水触发条件 KB_DRAFT_v1 makeup_water

metadata.source_document: KB_DRAFT_v1

source_document: KB_DRAFT_v1
text:
补水水质与参数要求
Makeup water for the expansion tank must meet specified quality standards, including pH (typically 6.5-8.5), chloride content (<50 ppm), and total hardness (<10 ppm) to prevent corrosion and scaling in the cooling system. The makeup flow rate is usually designed to be 1-2% of the main cooling water flow rate, with a minimum pressure of 0.2 MPa to overcome system backpressure.
search_text: 补水水质与参数要求 KB_DRAFT_v1 makeup_water <50 <10 2%

metadata.source_document: KB_DRAFT_v1

tier_reason: 描述性测试步骤，无强制约束
source_document: KB_DRAFT_v1
text:
验证与测试方法
During commissioning or periodic testing, the makeup water system is verified by simulating a low-level condition (e.g., draining the tank to the alarm setpoint) and confirming that the makeup valve opens and refills the tank to the normal level within a specified time (e.g., 5 minutes). Additionally, a makeup water meter or sight glass is used to check for continuous leakage or excessive makeup demand, which may indicate system leaks or pump seal failures.
search_text: 验证与测试方法 KB_DRAFT_v1 makeup_water 背景

source_document: KB_DRAFT_v1
text:
过滤器压降触发清洗条件
For seawater cooling systems, the pressure drop across the filter should be monitored. When the pressure drop exceeds 0.1 bar (or the manufacturer's specified limit), the filter requires cleaning or backflushing. This threshold is commonly used to prevent excessive strain on the cooling water pump and ensure adequate flow to the engine.
search_text: 过滤器压降触发清洗条件 KB_DRAFT_v1 pressure_drop 0.1bar

metadata.topic: 过滤器压降触发清洗条件
metadata.source_document: KB_DRAFT_v1

source_document: KB_DRAFT_v1
text:
过滤器压降设计参数要求
The design pressure drop of a clean filter in a main engine cooling water system is typically between 0.02 and 0.05 bar at design flow rate. The maximum allowable pressure drop before cleaning is usually 0.1-0.2 bar, depending on the system pressure and pump capacity. These values ensure efficient operation and avoid cavitation in the pump.
search_text: 过滤器压降设计参数要求 KB_DRAFT_v1 pressure_drop 0.05bar 0.2bar

source_document: KB_DRAFT_v1
text:
过滤器压降验证方法
Pressure drop across the filter is verified by installing differential pressure gauges or transmitters across the filter inlet and outlet. During commissioning, the pressure drop at design flow is recorded as baseline. Periodic checks are performed, and if the pressure drop exceeds the alarm setpoint (e.g., 0.15 bar), maintenance is triggered. This method aligns with CCS, DNV, and ABS requirements for cooling water system monitoring.

text:
报警触发条件与设定值文件要求
The alarm system documentation must include a complete list of alarm set points and their triggering conditions, such as high temperature, low pressure, or overspeed. For each alarm, the manufacturer's manual should specify the sensor type, location, and the logic for activation (e.g., delay time, voting logic). This ensures that the alarm system can be properly calibrated and tested during commissioning and maintenance.

图纸与接线图文件要求
The documentation shall provide detailed electrical schematic diagrams and wiring diagrams for the alarm system, covering all sensors, control units, and actuators. These drawings must clearly indicate cable types, terminal numbers, and signal flow. Additionally, a system block diagram showing the interface with the main engine control system and other ship systems is required to facilitate troubleshooting and system integration.

text:
备件目录与维护手册要求
The spare parts catalog for the alarm system must list all replaceable components, including sensors, relays, fuses, and display units, with part numbers and recommended stock levels. The maintenance manual should include periodic testing procedures, calibration intervals, and troubleshooting guides. This documentation supports the ship's planned maintenance system and ensures availability of critical spares for alarm system reliability.
